title: Private deployments customer requirements, reference architectures, on-prem packaging, day-2 ops, upgrade & rollback
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This page consolidates the customer requirements library, reference architectures, on-prem packaging checklist, day-2 operations runbooks, and upgrade/rollback procedures used by Redwood Inference for private (VPC and on-prem) deployments. It is intended as the canonical operations and pre-sales reference for Solutions, SRE, and Customer Engineering.

Audience:
- Customer Engineering and Solutions architects
- Platform and SRE teams responsible for Private deployments
- Security & Compliance reviewers

Scope:
Covers both VPC-based private deployments (cloud-hosted in customer VPCs) and fully on-prem packaged deployments. Includes guidance for initial deployment, day-2 operations, and safe upgrades with rollback.

1) Customer Requirements Library (summary)

High-level requirement categories and minimums we validate during onboarding. Use this as a checklist in pre-sales and kickoff.

Network & Connectivity:
- Dedicated VPC or VLAN with documented CIDR ranges
- Cross-account IAM role (cloud) or service account footprint (on-prem)
- Ports: 443 (API), 9411 (tracing), 9100 (metrics), 22 (bastion, optional)
- Egress policy allowing Redwood control-plane endpoints for optional telemetry (if customer consents)

Compute & Storage:
- Minimum GPU profile (if serving on customer infra): 1x A10G or equivalent per model shard; reference sizes documented in Reference Architectures section
- Persistent storage for state (KV cache), recommended NFS or distributed block with >= 500GB for medium workloads
- Ephemeral SSD for container local storage (>= 200GB)

Security & Compliance:
- KMS/HSM integration for customer-managed keys (cloud KMS or on-prem HSM)
- Audit logging enabled for all control-plane actions; retention SLA: 90 days (configurable)
- Network segmentation for admin plane and data plane

Observability & Monitoring:
- Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoint and recommended retention (90d)
- Tracing (Jaeger or OTEL) with sampling default 1% and adjustable per-customer
- Log aggregation via syslog/EFK-compatible endpoint

Operational Policies:
- Backup schedule for configuration and KV cache snapshots: daily incremental + weekly full
- Snapshot retention: 30 days by default
- SLOs agreed in contract (typical: P99 latency target 300ms for cached requests, 1500ms uncached, availability 99.9%)

Acceptance Criteria (final checklist before handoff):
- All monitoring dashboards present and green for 48h
- Canary traffic run for 24h with no errors >0.5%
- Security review completed and evidence uploaded to customer portal

2) Reference Architectures

A. VPC Private Deployment (cloud-hosted in customer VPC)

Topology summary:
- Control plane: run in Redwood-managed account (optionally customer-managed control plane for high-compliance cases).
- Data plane: deployed into customer VPC subnets across at least 2 AZs for redundancy.
- Ingress: ALB/NLB (TLS termination per customer choice); API endpoints fronted by customer API Gateway if required.
- Internal services: Kubernetes (EKS/GKE/AKS) or self-hosted k8s, with dedicated node pools for serving (GPU) and control services (CPU).

Minimum sizing guidance (example for baseline production):
- Serving pool: 3 x GPU nodes (A10G) with 48 vCPU, 384GB RAM each (handles ~200 concurrent low-latency sessions)
- Control plane: 3 x m5.large-equivalent for API & orchestration
- Storage: 1TB NVMe for model cache per AZ + shared NFS for state

Resilience & routing:
- Autoscaling configured for serving with minimum 2 replicas per AZ and burst policy to add 2 in 5m windows
- Smart routing: local region preference + fallback to lower-cost model variant if capacity constrained (configured in routing policy manifest)

B. On-prem Packaged Deployment

Topology summary:
- Appliance-style deployment using k8s distribution (RKE2 or upstream k8s supported).
- All components delivered as Helm charts + OCI images in an air-gapped bundle (tarball + signed artifacts).
- Optional hardware appliance reference: 4 x GPU servers (A100 or equivalent), 2 x control nodes, 10GbE network, redundant power

Air-gap considerations:
- All container images signed and verified at install-time using cosign.
- Offline license/key provisioning tool included; KMS sync adapter for HSM integration

3) On-prem Packaging Checklist (installer & bundle requirements)

Installer artifacts (must be present in release bundle):
- Helm charts (versions pinned), values templates, and sample values.yaml
- Signed OCI image bundle (sha256 checksums file) and installer script
- Post-install verification scripts (healthcheck, sample inference tests)
- Uninstall scripts and explicit rollback artifact (previous Helm release bundle)

Prereqs validated by Customer Engineering during install:
- Minimum OS version and kernel settings (documented in README)
- Required kernel modules for GPU passthrough and NVMe drivers
- NTP/synchronized time source

Packaging notes for Field Engineers:
- Provide both online and offline installation modes.
- Provide automated configuration validation (preflight) that returns explicit remediation steps.

4) Day-2 Operations Runbook

Expected monitoring & alerting configuration (recommended):
- Alerts: CPU/GPU utilization > 85% sustained 5m, P99 latency breach > target, model load failures > 1% per hour, disk usage > 80%
- Severity mapping: Sev1 (service unavailable), Sev2 (P99 SLO breach), Sev3 (degraded but within SLOs)

Daily operational checklist:
1. Review alert dashboard (top 5 active alerts)
2. Confirm control-plane sync & model catalog consistency
3. Validate backups completed and perform spot-restore test weekly
4. Check KV cache eviction rates and hit ratio (target > 70% for cache-friendly workloads)

Scaling guidance:
- Horizontal scale serving pods for concurrency by +20% when CPU steady-state >70% and queue length > 200 requests
- Vertical scale (increase model shard size) only after verifying throughput benefits and memory headroom

Backup and restore steps (high level):
1. Initiate config snapshot: kubectl exec -n redwood control-plane -- /opt/redwood/bin/snapshot --type=config
2. Verify snapshot checksum and upload to customer S3 or on-prem artifact store
3. To restore: pause ingestion, apply snapshot via restore CLI, validate service state pre-traffic

5) Upgrade and Rollback Procedures

Principles:
- Always test upgrades in a staging environment that mirrors production (same model catalog and traffic profile).
- Use canary rollouts with traffic shifting (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and automated health checks.
- Keep at least one known-good release bundle available for immediate rollback.

Pre-upgrade checklist:
- Backups: full config + KV cache snapshot within last 24h
- Health: all Sev1/Sev2 alerts resolved for 72h
- Observability: synthetic canary tests passing for 24h
- Release notes and migration steps validated with Customer Engineering

Canary rollout steps (Kubernetes/Helm example):
1. Deploy new Helm release to a canary subset: helm upgrade --install redwood-serving-canary ./charts/serving --set replicaCount=1 --set canary=true --values canary-values.yaml
2. Route 10% of production traffic to canary using traffic-split (Contour/Ingress) or service mesh route rules
3. Monitor key metrics for 30m: error rate, P99 latency, GPU utilization, memory usage
4. If metrics stable, increase traffic to 50% for 30m, then 100% and promote release

Rollback procedure (immediate):
1. Cut traffic to canary: update route to send 0% to canary
2. helm rollback redwood-serving <previous-release> --namespace redwood
3. If cluster-level issue, run emergency rollback script: /opt/redwood/bin/emergency-rollback --bundle /artifacts/redwood-release-previous.tgz
4. Post-rollback: run validation suite and create an incident timeline for RCA

6) Incident playbook (P99 latency spike example)

Trigger: sustained P99 latency > contract SLO for 15 minutes.

Immediate steps (first 15 minutes):
1. Pager duty: oncall SE and SRE respond.
2. Triage: Check serving pod logs, GPU saturation, OOMs, and queue backlog.
3. Short-term mitigation: scale serving pool (kubectl scale deployment redwood-serving --replicas=<n+2>) and enable fallback model variant if configured.
4. Notify customer CS contact with initial status and ETA.

Post-incident (within 24-72h):
- Produce postmortem, include timeline, actions, and follow-up changes.
- If root cause is model regression, mark model as quarantined in model catalog and roll back to previous model version.

7) Ownership, contacts & escalations

Default owners:
- Private Deployments (Customer Engineering): team-private-deployments@redwood.ai
- SRE escalation: eng-sre-oncall@redwood.ai (pager via PD)
- Security contact: security-oncall@redwood.ai

Escalation matrix:
- 0-15m: Oncall SE handles mitigation
- 15-60m: SRE engaged for cluster-level actions
- 60m+: Engineering leadership and Customer Success engaged for customer communications

8) Appendix useful commands & snippets

Health check (sample):
- kubectl get pods -n redwood -o wide
- kubectl logs -n redwood deployment/redwood-serving --tail=200

Snapshot (sample):
- /opt/redwood/bin/snapshot --type=config --out /tmp/config-snap.tar.gz
- sha256sum /tmp/config-snap.tar.gz

Helm canary promotion (sample):
- kubectl apply -f traffic-split-10-to-canary.yaml
- (monitor) kubectl get hpa -n redwood

Packaging validation (preflight):
- ./install.sh --preflight --bundle redwood-offline-bundle-vX.tgz --output preflight-report.json
